kind.description: Only Handles of this kind: ``frame``, ``profile``, ``routing``, ``recipe``, ``unit``, ``imputer`` or ``c2st``. Null lists every kind.

offset.description: How many of the newest Handles to skip, for the next page. Null means 0. Constraints: at least 0.

limit.description: Most Handles to return, from 1 to 12. Null means 12. Constraints: at least 1; at most 12.

output.description: One page of Handles, newest first, with their Lineage.

warnings.description: Caveats on this result, most actionable first. Empty when there are none.

fields.description: Always exactly `code`, `message`, `columns`, `param`, `hint`, in this order. A row's value at position i is the field named here at i.

rows.description: A caveat on a successful result: it worked, but read this first. One row per record, its values in `fields` order. The i-th schema below describes position i.

anyOf.description: Position 0, `code`: The warning's Error Code. Branch on this, not on ``message``.
Position 1, `message`: What happened and what to do, in one or two sentences.
Position 2, `columns`: Columns the warning concerns, or null.
Position 3, `param`: The argument the warning concerns, or null.
Position 4, `hint`: Library-written advice, or null.

omitted.description: One entry per list that was cut, naming the Operation that returns the rest. Empty when nothing was cut.

fields.description: Always exactly `field`, `shown`, `total`, `operation`, `reason`, in this order. A row's value at position i is the field named here at i.

rows.description: Something left out of a result: a capped list was cut, or a Literal Field withheld. One row per record, its values in `fields` order. The i-th schema below describes position i.

anyOf.description: Position 0, `field`: Name of the list field that was cut, or the path of the Literal Field withheld, such as ``top_values[].value``.
Position 1, `shown`: How many items the list holds; 0 for a withheld Literal Field or cut cells.
Position 2, `total`: How many items exist; for a withheld Literal Field, how many values at that path are null; for cut cells, how many were cut.
Position 3, `operation`: The Operation that returns the rest, or null when no Operation does.
Position 4, `reason`: ``cap`` when a list was cut to its cap; ``literal_policy`` when the Operator's Literal Policy is ``deny``; ``truncated`` when long text cells were cut to their character cap.

total.description: How many Handles of the asked kind exist in the Workspace.

offset.description: How many of the newest Handles this page skipped.

handles.description: Handles, newest first. At most 12; when more remain, ``omitted`` counts them and names ``list_handles``.

fields.description: Always exactly `handle`, `kind`, `operation`, `arguments`, `inputs`, `size`, in this order. A row's value at position i is the field named here at i.

rows.description: One Handle and its Lineage: what made it, from what, with which arguments. One row per record, its values in `fields` order. The i-th schema below describes position i.

anyOf.description: Position 0, `handle`: The Handle, such as ``frame_7f3a9c2e``. Pass it to any Operation that takes this kind.
Position 1, `kind`: The Handle's kind: the prefix before the underscore.
Position 2, `operation`: The Operation that made the Handle.
Position 3, `arguments`: The arguments that Operation was called with, as passed. Arguments left at their default are absent.

fields.description: Always exactly `name`, `value`, `value_cut`, in this order. A row's value at position i is the field named here at i.

rows.description: One argument the Operation that made the Handle was called with. One row per record, its values in `fields` order. The i-th schema below describes position i.

anyOf.description: Position 0, `name`: Argument name, as in that Operation's signature.
Position 1, `value`: The value as passed, as JSON text. Cut at 80 characters, ending in ``…``, when ``value_cut`` is true.
Position 2, `value_cut`: True when ``value`` was cut and is not valid JSON.
Position 4, `inputs`: The Handles that Operation read, in the order it read them. At most 10; past 10, ``omitted`` counts the rest.
Position 5, `size`: A short size summary, such as rows and columns for a frame.

fields.description: Always exactly `measure`, `value`, in this order. A row's value at position i is the field named here at i.

rows.description: One measure of a Handle's size. One row per record, its values in `fields` order. The i-th schema below describes position i.

anyOf.description: Position 0, `measure`: What is counted, such as ``rows`` or ``columns``.
Position 1, `value`: The count.
